title: 149. Detect Squares

examples.explanation: Only count operations contribute entries to the returned array.
The duplicate [11,2] is a distinct choice and doubles the second count.
The count of squares for the query is [0].

hints: This is a function adaptation, not a class problem: skip the first constructor row and append results only for count operations.
Store the multiplicity of every added point; duplicate points must multiply the number of square choices.
For a query [x,y], enumerate stored points [otherX,y] on the same row. Their horizontal distance determines the only two possible opposite rows.
Multiply the frequencies of the three required stored corners for each possible square.
